Title: What prohibits from burning an Edge you don't control?

Messages.Body:

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body: I would say, the same thing prevent you from burning an edge you don't control that prevent you from burning pool you don't own.

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
> Ankha wrote:
> I can't find any rule reference for that matter.
>
> Name: Lucinde, Alastor
> Camarilla Ventrue Justicar: Lucinde can enter combat with any ready non-Camarilla vampire controlled by another Methuselah as a  action. During your untap phase, you can burn the Edge to give Lucinde 1 blood from the blood bank.

I can't find it either.

"Burn the Edge" effects are only usable if you control the Edge (unless otherwise specified).

This applies to: 419 Operation, Alonzo Guillen, Deploy the Hand, Emily Carson, Eric Kressida, Extorsion, Hartmut Stover, High Priestess Angra Mainyu, Isouda de Blaise, Lady Constancia, Leverage, Lucinde, Alastor, Mapatano Utando, Powerbase: Zürich, Sabbat Threat, Sarrasine, Shatter the Gate, Soldat, Torvus Bloodbeard, Tragic Love Affair, Victoria and Victorine Lafourcade.

Messages.Author: KevinM
Messages.Body:

And 1.1.2 & 6.3.3 define "burning the edge" as you must have the edge to burn it.

Messages.Author: Boris The Blade
Messages.Body:
It's not about the edge, it is about paying costs. One could imagine a card like that:

Reset
+1 stealth action.
Burn the edge.

That would burn the edge no matter where it is on the table. (Please don't print that, we have enough crappy cards with the edge already )

But IIRC there is currently no such effect. All effects that require edge burning do so as a cost ("burn the edge to..."). The general rule should be: you can only pay a cost with resources you own/control.

The analogy with pool is: your actions can burn someone else's pool, but the cost must be paid from your pool.
